reason: While the text clearly portrays the Israelites (בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל) as a unified nation and organized people (כָּל־ עֲדַ֨ת), this passage describes them traveling through the wilderness of Sin (מִמִּדְבַּר־ סִ֛ין) and camping at Rephidim. The text depicts them as a nomadic people in transit through desert territory, not as a nation possessing or dwelling in their own specific land. They are between Egypt and their eventual destination, not portrayed as inhabitants of established territory.
